core: Narrative as the organization and disclosure of story information in moving-image works
Story and plot, cause and consequence, goals and obstacles, and restricted or broader narration
Temporal ordering, including flashbacks and flashforwards, as an observable storytelling choice
supporting: The relationship among protagonist, goal, obstacles, conflict, and changing information
Boundaries among narrative, theme, genre, character, editing, cinematography, and sound
A method for tracing what viewers know and when they receive it
outOfScope: Screenwriting formulas, prescriptive plot templates, or personalized creative-writing advice
A complete survey of genre or an interpretation of a particular copyrighted film
Claims that every narrative follows three acts or that one ordering has a universal audience effect

claims.claim: Narrative analysis asks how a moving-image work organizes and reveals story information, including what viewers know, what is withheld, and how elements are ordered.
A basic narrative model can identify a central character pursuing a goal while encountering obstacles, but this model is a useful pattern rather than a rule every work must follow.
Plot can be analyzed as the presented sequence of events, while story analysis also considers relationships, chronology, and information viewers infer beyond what is directly shown.
Narration can be comparatively restricted around one character's knowledge or broadened to provide viewers with information from multiple characters and locations.
Flashbacks, flashforwards, and other changes in ordering can alter when viewers receive information without necessarily changing the underlying chronology of events.
Narrative is carried through coordinated image, sound, performance, staging, and editing choices rather than through plot summary alone.

A responsible narrative interpretation maps events and information, identifies a supported pattern of goals, obstacles, or disclosure, and makes a qualified claim rather than imposing a formula or private intent.

unsupportedExistingClaims: No usable lesson, evidence packet, or source-linked four-option question set existed for this planned narrative topic.
